questions.text: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function. If the domain of the function $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x+[x]}{3}\right)$ is $[\alpha,\beta)$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Need $-3\le x+[x]\le3$. Write $x=n+f$, $n=[x]$, $0\le f<1$: $-3\le 2n+f\le3$.
$n=1$: $2+f\le3$ always holds, so $[1,2)$ works; $n=2$ gives $4+f>3$ (fails).
$n=-1$: $-2+f\ge-3$ holds, so $[-1,0)$ works; $n=-2$ needs $f\ge1$ (fails). $n=0$ works.
Domain $=[-1,2)$, so $\alpha=-1$, $\beta=2$ and $\alpha^2+\beta^2=5$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let one root of the quadratic equation in $x$:
$(k^2-15k+27)x^2+9(k-1)x+18=0$
be twice the other. Then the length of the latus rectum of the parabola $y^2=6kx$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Let $A=k^2-15k+27$ and the roots be $r,2r$.
Sum: $3r=-\dfrac{9(k-1)}{A}$; product: $2r^2=\dfrac{18}{A}\Rightarrow r^2=\dfrac{9}{A}$.
From the sum, $9r^2=\dfrac{81(k-1)^2}{A^2}$, so $\dfrac{81}{A}=\dfrac{81(k-1)^2}{A^2}\Rightarrow A=(k-1)^2$.
$k^2-15k+27=k^2-2k+1\Rightarrow 13k=26\Rightarrow k=2$.
Parabola $y^2=12x$: latus rectum $=12$.

questions.text:
Let $e_1$ and $e_2$ be two distinct roots of the equation $x^2-ax+2=0$. Let the sets
$\{a\in\mathbb{R}: e_1 \text{ and } e_2 \text{ are the eccentricities of hyperbolas}\}=(\alpha,\beta)$, and
$\{a\in\mathbb{R}: e_1 \text{ and } e_2 \text{ are the eccentricities of an ellipse and a hyperbola, respectively}\}=(\gamma,\infty)$.
Then $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Let $f(x)=x^2-ax+2$, with $f(0)=2>0$.
Both roots $>1$ (two hyperbolas): $a^2>8$, $f(1)=3-a>0$, $\dfrac a2>1$, so $a\in(2\sqrt2,3)$: $\alpha=2\sqrt2$, $\beta=3$.
One root in $(0,1)$ and one $>1$: $f(1)=3-a<0\Rightarrow a>3$, so $\gamma=3$.
$\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=8+9+9=26$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the set of all values of $k\in\mathbb{R}$ such that the equation $z(\bar z+2+i)+k(2+3i)=0$, $z\in\mathbb{C}$, has at least one solution, be the interval $[\alpha,\beta]$. Then $9(\alpha+\beta)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Put $z=x+iy$: $|z|^2+(2+i)z+k(2+3i)=0$, and $(2+i)z=(2x-y)+i(x+2y)$.
Real part: $x^2+y^2+2x-y+2k=0$, a circle with centre $\left(-1,\dfrac12\right)$ and $r^2=\dfrac54-2k$.
Imaginary part: $x+2y+3k=0$, a line.
A solution exists iff the line meets the circle: $\dfrac{|-1+1+3k|}{\sqrt5}\le\sqrt{\dfrac54-2k}\iff 36k^2+40k-25\le0$.
So $\alpha+\beta$ is the sum of the roots $=-\dfrac{40}{36}=-\dfrac{10}{9}$, and $9(\alpha+\beta)=-10$.

questions.text: The sum of the first ten terms of an A.P. is 160 and the sum of the first two terms of a G.P. is 8. If the first term of the A.P. is equal to the common ratio of the G.P. and the first term of the G.P. is equal to common difference of the A.P., then the sum of all possible values of the first term of the G.P. is:
questions.sol:
A.P.: first term $a$, difference $d$: $5(2a+9d)=160\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{32-9d}{2}$.
G.P.: first term $d$, ratio $a$: $d(1+a)=8\Rightarrow d\cdot\dfrac{34-9d}{2}=8$.
$9d^2-34d+16=0$ (real roots, discriminant $1156-576>0$).
Sum of the possible first terms $d$ of the G.P. $=\dfrac{34}{9}$.

questions.text: The number of 4-letter words, with or without meaning, each consisting of two vowels and two consonants that can be formed from the letters of the word INCONSEQUENTIAL, without repeating any letter, is:
questions.sol:
Distinct vowels: I, O, E, U, A (5). Distinct consonants: N, C, S, Q, T, L (6).
Choose 2 vowels and 2 consonants, all different, and arrange: $\binom52\binom62\,4!=10\times15\times24=3600$.

questions.text: If the coefficients of the middle terms in the binomial expansions of $(1+\alpha x)^{26}$ and $(1-\alpha x)^{28}$, $\alpha\ne0$, are equal, then the value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.sol:
Middle term of $(1+\alpha x)^{26}$: $T_{14}$, coefficient $\binom{26}{13}\alpha^{13}$.
Middle term of $(1-\alpha x)^{28}$: $T_{15}$, coefficient $\binom{28}{14}\alpha^{14}$.
Equal: $\alpha=\dfrac{\binom{26}{13}}{\binom{28}{14}}=\dfrac{14\cdot14}{28\cdot27}=\dfrac{7}{27}$.

questions.text: A data consists of 20 observations $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{20}$. If $\sum_{i=1}^{20}(x_i+5)^2=2500$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{20}(x_i-5)^2=100$, then the ratio of mean to standard deviation of this data is:
questions.sol:
Subtracting: $20\sum x_i=2400\Rightarrow\sum x_i=120$, mean $=6$.
Adding: $2\sum x_i^2+2\cdot20\cdot25=2600\Rightarrow\sum x_i^2=800$.
Variance $=\dfrac{800}{20}-36=4$, so $\sigma=2$.
Mean : SD $=6:2=3:1$.

questions.text: A bag contains $(N+1)$ coins $-$ $N$ fair coins, and one coin with 'Head' on both sides. A coin is selected at random and tossed. If the probability of getting 'Head' is $\dfrac{9}{16}$, then $N$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$P(H)=\dfrac{N}{N+1}\cdot\dfrac12+\dfrac{1}{N+1}\cdot1=\dfrac{N+2}{2(N+1)}$.
$\dfrac{N+2}{2(N+1)}=\dfrac9{16}\Rightarrow16N+32=18N+18\Rightarrow N=7$.

questions.text: If the eccentricity $e$ of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, passing through $(6,4\sqrt3)$, satisfies $15(e^2+1)=34e$, then the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{b^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{2(a^2+1)}=1$ is:
questions.sol:
$15e^2-34e+15=0\Rightarrow e=\dfrac53$ (since $e>1$), so $\dfrac{b^2}{a^2}=e^2-1=\dfrac{16}{9}$.
Through $(6,4\sqrt3)$: $\dfrac{36}{a^2}-\dfrac{48\cdot9}{16a^2}=\dfrac{9}{a^2}=1\Rightarrow a^2=9$, $b^2=16$.
Second hyperbola: $\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}{20}=1$, latus rectum $=\dfrac{2\cdot20}{4}=10$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let chord PQ of length $3\sqrt{13}$ of the parabola $y^2=12x$ be such that the ordinates of points P and Q are in the ratio $1:2$. If the chord PQ subtends an angle $\alpha$ at the focus of the parabola, then $\sin\alpha$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Take $P(3t^2,6t)$, $Q(12t^2,12t)$ (ordinates in ratio $1:2$).
$PQ^2=81t^4+36t^2=117\Rightarrow9t^4+4t^2-13=0\Rightarrow t^2=1$.
With $t=1$: $P(3,6)$, $Q(12,12)$, focus $S(3,0)$; $\vec{SP}=(0,6)$, $\vec{SQ}=(9,12)$.
$\cos\alpha=\dfrac{72}{6\cdot15}=\dfrac45\Rightarrow\sin\alpha=\dfrac35$ ($t=-1$ is the mirror image).
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $0<\alpha<1$, $\beta=\dfrac{1}{3\alpha}$ and $\tan^{-1}(1-\alpha)+\tan^{-1}(1-\beta)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. Then $6(\alpha+\beta)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{(1-\alpha)+(1-\beta)}{1-(1-\alpha)(1-\beta)}=1\Rightarrow2-\alpha-\beta=\alpha+\beta-\alpha\beta$.
$2(\alpha+\beta)=2+\alpha\beta=2+\dfrac13=\dfrac73\Rightarrow\alpha+\beta=\dfrac76$.
(Check: $\alpha+\dfrac1{3\alpha}=\dfrac76$ gives $\alpha=\dfrac12$ or $\dfrac23$, both in $(0,1)$.)
$6(\alpha+\beta)=7$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $S=\left\{\theta\in(-2\pi,2\pi):\cos\theta+1=\sqrt3\sin\theta\right\}$. Then $\sum_{\theta\in S}\theta$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$\sqrt3\sin\theta-\cos\theta=1\Rightarrow\sin\left(\theta-\dfrac\pi6\right)=\dfrac12$.
$\theta-\dfrac\pi6=\dfrac\pi6+2n\pi$ or $\dfrac{5\pi}6+2n\pi$, i.e. $\theta=\dfrac\pi3+2n\pi$ or $\theta=\pi+2n\pi$.
In $(-2\pi,2\pi)$: $\dfrac\pi3,-\dfrac{5\pi}3,\pi,-\pi$.
Sum $=\dfrac\pi3-\dfrac{5\pi}3=-\dfrac{4\pi}3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the image of the point $P(1,6,a)$ in the line $L:\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-a+1}{b}$, $b>0$, be $\left(\dfrac a3,0,a+c\right)$. If $S(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$, $\alpha>0$, is the point on $L$ such that the distance of $S$ from the foot of perpendicular from the point $P$ on $L$ is $2\sqrt{14}$, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
A point of $L$ is $(t,1+2t,a-1+bt)$. The midpoint of $P$ and its image is $\left(\dfrac{1+a/3}{2},3,\dfrac{2a+c}{2}\right)$ and lies on $L$.
$y$: $1+2t=3\Rightarrow t=1$; $x$: $\dfrac{1+a/3}{2}=1\Rightarrow a=3$; $z$: $2+b=\dfrac{6+c}{2}\Rightarrow c=2b-2$.
$P'-P=(0,-6,c)$ is perpendicular to $(1,2,b)$: $-12+bc=0\Rightarrow b(2b-2)=12\Rightarrow b=3$, $c=4$.
Foot $M=(1,3,5)$, direction $(1,2,3)$ with length $\sqrt{14}$, so $S=M\pm2(1,2,3)$.
$\alpha>0$: $S=(3,7,11)$, and $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=21$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let a line L be perpendicular to both the lines $L_1:\dfrac{x+1}{3}=\dfrac{y+3}{5}=\dfrac{z+5}{7}$ and $L_2:\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y-4}{4}=\dfrac{z-6}{7}$.
If $\theta$ is the acute angle between the lines L and $L_3:\dfrac{x-\frac87}{2}=\dfrac{y-\frac47}{1}=\dfrac{z}{2}$, then $\tan\theta$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Direction of L: $(3,5,7)\times(1,4,7)=(7,-14,7)\parallel(1,-2,1)$.
Direction of $L_3$: $(2,1,2)$.
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{|2-2+2|}{\sqrt6\cdot3}=\dfrac{2}{3\sqrt6}$, so $\sin\theta=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{4}{54}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{50}}{3\sqrt6}$.
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{50}}{2}=\dfrac52\sqrt2$.

questions.text: The value of $\lim\limits_{x\to0}\left(\dfrac{x^2\sin^2x}{x^2-\sin^2x}\right)$ is:
questions.sol:
$\sin^2x=x^2-\dfrac{x^4}{3}+O(x^6)$, so $x^2-\sin^2x=\dfrac{x^4}{3}+O(x^6)$.
Numerator $x^2\sin^2x=x^4+O(x^6)$.
Limit $=\dfrac{1}{1/3}=3$.

questions.text: The value of the integral $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4}\left(\dfrac{32\cos^4x}{1+e^{\sin x}}\right)dx$ is:
questions.sol:
Replacing $x$ by $-x$ and adding: $2I=\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4}32\cos^4x\,dx$, so $I=32\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\cos^4x\,dx$.
$\cos^4x=\dfrac{3+4\cos2x+\cos4x}{8}$, and $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\cos^4x\,dx=\dfrac18\left(\dfrac{3\pi}4+2+0\right)$.
$I=4\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}+2\right)=3\pi+8$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The area of the region $\{(x,y):0\le y\le6-x,\ y^2\ge4x-3,\ x\ge0\}$ is:
questions.sol:
For $y\ge0$ the region is $0\le x\le\min\left(\dfrac{y^2+3}{4},\,6-y\right)$.
The curves meet where $y^2+3=24-4y\Rightarrow y=3$; below $y=3$ the parabola is the smaller bound.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_0^3\dfrac{y^2+3}{4}dy+\int_3^6(6-y)\,dy=\dfrac{9+9}{4}+\dfrac92=9$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $e$ be the base of natural logarithm and let $f:\{1,2,3,4\}\to\{1,e,e^2,e^3\}$ and $g:\{1,e,e^2,e^3\}\to\left\{1,\dfrac12,\dfrac13,\dfrac14\right\}$ be two bijective functions such that $f$ is strictly decreasing and $g$ is strictly increasing. If $\phi(x)=\left[f^{-1}\left\{g^{-1}\left(\dfrac12\right)\right\}\right]^x$, then the area of the region $R=\{(x,y):x^2\le y\le\phi(x),\ 0\le x\le1\}$ is:
questions.sol:
$g$ increasing: $g(1)=\dfrac14$, $g(e)=\dfrac13$, $g(e^2)=\dfrac12$, $g(e^3)=1$, so $g^{-1}\left(\dfrac12\right)=e^2$.
$f$ decreasing: $f(1)=e^3$, $f(2)=e^2$, so $f^{-1}(e^2)=2$ and $\phi(x)=2^x$.
$2^x\ge x^2$ on $[0,1]$: area $=\displaystyle\int_0^1(2^x-x^2)\,dx=\dfrac{1}{\ln2}-\dfrac13=\dfrac{3-\log_e2}{3\log_e2}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}-1&1&-1\\1&0&1\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$ satisfy $$A^2+\alpha\big(adj(adj(A))\big)+\beta\big(adj(A)\,(adj(adj(A)))\big)=\begin{bmatrix}2&-2&2\\-2&0&-1\\0&0&-1\end{bmatrix}$$ for some $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$.
Then $(\alpha-\beta)^2$ is equal to ________
questions.sol:
$|A|=-1(0)-1(1)+(-1)(0)=-1$.
$adj(adj A)=|A|^{n-2}A=-A$ and $adj(A)\,(adj(adj A))=-adj(A)A=-|A|I=I$.
$A^2=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&1\\-1&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$, so $A^2-\alpha A+\beta I$ must equal the given matrix.
Entry $(1,2)$: $-1-\alpha=-2\Rightarrow\alpha=1$; entry $(1,1)$: $2+\alpha+\beta=2\Rightarrow\beta=-1$ (all other entries agree).
$(\alpha-\beta)^2=4$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the centre of the circle $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+25=0$ be in the first quadrant and lie on the line $2x-y=4$. Let the area of an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle be $27\sqrt3$. Then the square of the length of the chord of the circle on the line $x=1$ is ________.
questions.sol:
Equilateral triangle in a circle of radius $r$: area $=\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{4}r^2=27\sqrt3\Rightarrow r^2=36$.
Centre $(h,2h-4)$: $r^2=h^2+(2h-4)^2-25=36\Rightarrow5h^2-16h-45=0\Rightarrow h=5$ (first quadrant).
Centre $(5,6)$, distance from $x=1$ is $4$.
Chord$^2=4(36-16)=80$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$, $\vec b=\hat j-\hat k$ and $\vec c$ be three vectors such that $\vec a\times\vec c=\vec b$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec c=3$, then $\vec c\cdot(\vec a-2\vec b)$ is equal to ________.
questions.sol:
$\vec b=\vec a\times\vec c$ is perpendicular to $\vec c$, so $\vec c\cdot\vec b=0$.
$\vec c\cdot(\vec a-2\vec b)=3-0=3$.
(Indeed $\vec c=\dfrac{3\vec a-\vec a\times\vec b}{|\vec a|^2}=\dfrac{5\hat i+2\hat j+2\hat k}{3}$.)
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: For the functions $f(\theta)=\alpha\tan^2\theta+\beta\cot^2\theta$, and $g(\theta)=\alpha\sin^2\theta+\beta\cos^2\theta$, $\alpha>\beta>0$, let $\min\limits_{0<\theta<\frac\pi2}f(\theta)=\max\limits_{0<\theta<\pi}g(\theta)$. If the first term of a G.P. is $\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2\beta}\right)$, its common ratio is $\left(\dfrac{2\beta}{\alpha}\right)$ and the sum of its first 10 terms is $\dfrac mn$, $\gcd(m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to ________.
questions.sol:
By AM-GM, $\min f=2\sqrt{\alpha\beta}$. $g=\beta+(\alpha-\beta)\sin^2\theta$ has maximum $\alpha$ (at $\theta=\dfrac\pi2$).
$2\sqrt{\alpha\beta}=\alpha\Rightarrow\alpha=4\beta$.
G.P.: first term $2$, ratio $\dfrac12$: $S_{10}=\dfrac{2(1-2^{-10})}{1/2}=\dfrac{1023}{256}$.
$m+n=1023+256=1279$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $$\left(x^2-x\sqrt{x^2-1}-1\right)dy+\left(y\left(x-\sqrt{x^2-1}\right)-x\right)dx=0,\ x\ge1.$$ If $y(1)=1$, then the greatest integer less than $y\left(\sqrt5\right)$ is ________.
questions.sol:
Let $s=\sqrt{x^2-1}$ and $u=x-s$, so $\dfrac1u=x+s$ and $x^2-1-xs=-su$.
The equation becomes $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{y}{s}=-\dfrac{x(x+s)}{s}$.
Integrating factor $e^{-\int dx/s}=\dfrac{1}{x+s}=u$: $\dfrac{d(yu)}{dx}=-\dfrac{x}{s}\Rightarrow yu=1-\sqrt{x^2-1}$ (using $y(1)=1$).
So $y=(1-\sqrt{x^2-1})(x+\sqrt{x^2-1})$, and $y(\sqrt5)=-(2+\sqrt5)\approx-4.24$.
As printed, this gives $-5$; the official final key gives $3$, which this equation does not lead to. Official answer: $3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.note: The official final key gives 3. Solving the equation exactly as printed gives y(√5) = −(2 + √5) ≈ −4.24, i.e. −5; the key is followed for marking.

questions.text: The density $\rho$ of a uniform cylinder is determined by measuring its mass $m$, length $l$ and diameter $d$. The measured values of $m$, $l$ and $d$ are $97.42\pm0.02$ g, $8.35\pm0.05$ mm and $20.20\pm0.02$ mm, respectively. Calculated percentage fractional error in $\rho$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$\rho=\dfrac{4m}{\pi d^2l}\Rightarrow\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}=\dfrac{\Delta m}{m}+\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}+2\dfrac{\Delta d}{d}$.
$=\dfrac{0.02}{97.42}+\dfrac{0.05}{8.35}+\dfrac{2\times0.02}{20.20}=0.00021+0.00599+0.00198=0.00817$.
Percentage error $\approx0.82\%$.

questions.text: The potential energy of a particle changes with distance $x$ from a fixed origin as $V=\dfrac{A\sqrt x}{x+B}$, where $A$ and $B$ are constant with appropriate dimensions. The dimensions of $AB$ are ________.
questions.sol:
$B$ is added to $x$, so $[B]=[\mathrm{L}]$.
$[V]=\dfrac{[A]\mathrm{L^{1/2}}}{\mathrm{L}}\Rightarrow[A]=[\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}}]\mathrm{L^{1/2}}=[\mathrm{ML^{5/2}T^{-2}}]$.
$[AB]=[\mathrm{M^1L^{7/2}T^{-2}}]$.

questions.text:
The rain drop of mass 1 g, starts with zero velocity from a height of 1 km. It hits the ground with a speed of 5 m/s. The work done by the unknown resistive force is ________ J.
(take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Work-energy theorem: $W_g+W_r=\Delta K$.
$W_g=mgh=10^{-3}\times10\times1000=10$ J; $\Delta K=\dfrac12\times10^{-3}\times25=0.0125$ J.
$W_r=0.0125-10=-9.9875\approx-9.98$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Two blocks ($P$ and $Q$) with respectively masses 2 kg and 1.5 kg are joined by a massless thread. These blocks are mounted on a frictionless pully which is fixed on the edge of a cube ($S$), as shown in the figure below. Block $P$ is positioned on the top surface which has no friction and block $Q$ is in contact with side-surface, having coefficient friction $\mu$. The cube ($S$) moves towards the right with acceleration of $\dfrac g2$, where $g$ is gravitational acceleration. During this movement the block $P$ and $Q$ remain stationary. The value of $\mu$ is ________.
(take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Both blocks move with the cube, acceleration $a=\dfrac g2=5$ m/s$^2$ to the right.
$P$ (smooth top): only the thread pulls it horizontally, so $T=m_Pa=2\times5=10$ N.
$Q$: the side face pushes it horizontally, $N=m_Qa=1.5\times5=7.5$ N.
Vertically for $Q$: $T+f=m_Qg\Rightarrow f=15-10=5$ N.
No slipping: $f\le\mu N\Rightarrow\mu\ge\dfrac{5}{7.5}=\dfrac23\approx0.67$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A lift of mass 1600 kg is supported by thick iron wire. If the maximum stress which the wire can withstand is $4\times10^8$ N/m$^2$ and its radius is 4 mm, then maximum acceleration the lift can take is ______ m/s$^2$.
(take $g=10$ m/s$^2$ and $\pi=3.14$)
questions.sol:
Area $=\pi r^2=3.14\times16\times10^{-6}=5.024\times10^{-5}$ m$^2$.
Maximum tension $T=4\times10^8\times5.024\times10^{-5}=20096$ N.
$T-mg=ma\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{20096}{1600}-10=2.56$ m/s$^2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A solid sphere of radius 4 cm and mass 5 kg is rotating (rotation axis is passing through the centre of the sphere) with an angular velocity of 1200 rpm. It is brought to rest in 10 s by applying a constant torque. The torque applied and the number of rotations it made before it comes to rest are _____ and ________ respectively.
questions.sol:
$I=\dfrac25MR^2=\dfrac25\times5\times(0.04)^2=0.0032$ kg m$^2$.
$\omega_0=1200$ rpm $=40\pi$ rad/s, so $\alpha=\dfrac{40\pi}{10}=4\pi$ rad/s$^2$.
$\tau=I\alpha=0.0128\,\pi$ Nm.
$\theta=\dfrac{\omega_0t}{2}=200\pi$ rad $=100$ rotations.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: A smooth inclined plane ends in a vertical circular loop, as shown in the figure. A small body is released from height $h$ as shown. If the body exerts a force of three times its weight on the plane at the highest point of circle then the height $h=\alpha R$. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
questions.sol:
At the top: $N+mg=\dfrac{mv^2}{R}$ with $N=3mg\Rightarrow v^2=4gR$.
Energy: $mgh=mg(2R)+\dfrac12mv^2=2mgR+2mgR$.
$h=4R$, so $\alpha=4$.

questions.text: The position of center of mass of three masses 2 kg, 3 kg and 15 kg placed with respect to mid point ($p$) of normal bisector, as shown in the figure is ________.
questions.sol:
Half base $=10\sin60^\circ=5\sqrt3$ m, height $=10\cos60^\circ=5$ m, so $p$ is $2.5$ m above the base.
With $p$ as origin: 2 kg at $(-5\sqrt3,-2.5)$, 3 kg at $(5\sqrt3,-2.5)$, 15 kg at $(0,2.5)$.
$x_{cm}=\dfrac{-10\sqrt3+15\sqrt3}{20}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}$.
$y_{cm}=\dfrac{-5-7.5+37.5}{20}=1.25$.

questions.text: The two wires $A$ and $B$ of equal cross-section but of different materials are joined together. The ratio of Young's modulus of wire $A$ and wire $B$ is 20/11. When the joined wire is kept under certain tension the elongations in the wires $A$ and $B$ are equal. If the length of wire $A$ is 2.2 m, then the length of wire $B$ is ________ m.
questions.sol:
Same tension and area: $\Delta L=\dfrac{FL}{AY}$, so equal elongations need $\dfrac{L_A}{Y_A}=\dfrac{L_B}{Y_B}$.
$L_B=L_A\dfrac{Y_B}{Y_A}=2.2\times\dfrac{11}{20}=1.21$ m.

questions.text: Two closed vessels of same volume are joined through a narrow tube and both vessels are filled with air of pressure 90 kPa and temperature 400 K. Keeping the temperature of one vessel constant at 400 K the second vessel temperature is raised to 500 K. The final pressure in the vessels is ________ kPa.
questions.sol:
Total moles are conserved and the final pressure $p$ is common: $\dfrac{2\times90\,V}{R\cdot400}=\dfrac{pV}{R\cdot400}+\dfrac{pV}{R\cdot500}$.
$0.45=p\left(\dfrac{1}{400}+\dfrac{1}{500}\right)=p\cdot\dfrac{9}{2000}\Rightarrow p=100$ kPa.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In interference experiment the path difference between two interfering waves at a point $A$ on the screen is $\lambda/3$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of these waves, and at another point $B$ the path difference is $\lambda/6$. The ratio of intensities at points $A$ and $B$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$I=4I_0\cos^2\dfrac\phi2$ with $\phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x$.
A: $\phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, $I_A=4I_0\cos^2 60^\circ=I_0$. B: $\phi=\dfrac\pi3$, $I_B=4I_0\cos^2 30^\circ=3I_0$.
$I_A:I_B=1/3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion. Its amplitude is $A$ and time period is 5 sec. The time required by it to move from $x=A$ to $x=\dfrac{A}{\sqrt2}$ is ________ sec.
questions.sol:
$x=A\cos\omega t$; $x=\dfrac{A}{\sqrt2}$ when $\omega t=\dfrac\pi4$.
$t=\dfrac{\pi/4}{2\pi/T}=\dfrac T8=\dfrac58$ s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A thin half ring of radius 35 cm is uniformly charged with a total charge of $Q$ coulomb. If the magnitude of the electric field at centre of the half ring is 100 V/m, then the value of $Q$ is ________ nC.
($\epsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}$ C$^2$/Nm$^2$ and $\pi=3.14$)
questions.sol:
For a half ring, $E=\dfrac{2k\lambda}{R}$ with $\lambda=\dfrac{Q}{\pi R}$, so $E=\dfrac{Q}{2\pi^2\epsilon_0R^2}$.
$Q=2\pi^2\epsilon_0R^2E=2\times9.86\times8.85\times10^{-12}\times0.1225\times100$.
$Q\approx2.14\times10^{-9}$ C $=2.14$ nC.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The maximum rated power of the LED is 2 mW and it is used in the circuit with input voltage of 5 V as shown in the figure below. The current through resistance $R_S$ is 0.5 mA.
The minimum value of the resistance of $R_S$, to ensure that the LED is not damaged is ________ k$\Omega$.
questions.sol:
The diode in series with $R=1$ k$\Omega$ is reverse biased, so that branch carries no current and the whole $0.5$ mA flows through the LED.
At its maximum rating, LED voltage $V=\dfrac PI=\dfrac{2\text{ mW}}{0.5\text{ mA}}=4$ V.
$R_S=\dfrac{5-4}{0.5\times10^{-3}}=2$ k$\Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A point light source emits E.M. waves in free space. A detector, placed at a distance of $L$ m, measures the intensity as $I_0$. The detector is now shifted to another location on the same spherical surface ensuring the angle between original location and new location as $45^\circ$. The measured intensity at new location will be ________.
questions.sol:
A point source radiates uniformly in all directions: $I=\dfrac{P}{4\pi L^2}$ depends only on the distance.
The new position is on the same sphere (same $L$), so the intensity is still $I_0$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A spherical interface lens of radius $R$ separates two media of refractive indices 1 and 1.4 respectively as shown in the figure below. A point source is placed at a distance of $4R$ in front of spherical interface. The magnitude of the magnification of point source image is ________.
questions.sol:
Convex surface facing the source: $u=-4R$, radius $+R$, $n_1=1$, $n_2=1.4$.
$\dfrac{1.4}{v}-\dfrac{1}{-4R}=\dfrac{0.4}{R}\Rightarrow\dfrac{1.4}{v}=\dfrac{0.15}{R}\Rightarrow v=\dfrac{28R}{3}$.
$m=\dfrac{n_1v}{n_2u}=\dfrac{28R/3}{1.4\times(-4R)}=-\dfrac53$, so $|m|\approx1.66$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A small cube of side 1 mm is placed at the centre of a circular loop of radius 10 cm carrying a current of 2 A. The magnetic energy stored inside the cube is $\alpha\times10^{-14}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
($\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ Tm/A, $\pi=3.14$)
questions.sol:
$B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2R}=\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times2}{0.2}=4\pi\times10^{-6}$ T.
Energy density $u=\dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0}=\dfrac{16\pi^2\times10^{-12}}{8\pi\times10^{-7}}=2\pi\times10^{-5}$ J/m$^3$.
Energy $=u\times10^{-9}=2\pi\times10^{-14}=6.28\times10^{-14}$ J, so $\alpha=6.28$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An inductor of inductance 10 mH having resistance of 100 $\Omega$ is connected to battery of E.M.F. 1.0 V through a switch as shown in the figure below. After switch is closed, the ratio of instantaneous voltages across the inductor when the current passing through it is 2 mA and 4 mA is ________.
questions.sol:
Voltage across the inductive part: $V_L=E-iR$.
$i=2$ mA: $V_L=1-0.2=0.8$ V; $i=4$ mA: $V_L=1-0.4=0.6$ V.
Ratio $=\dfrac{0.8}{0.6}=\dfrac43$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The ratio of momentum of the photons of the 1$^{\text{st}}$ and 2$^{\text{nd}}$ line of Balmer series of Hydrogen atoms is $\alpha/\beta$. The possible values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are:-
questions.sol:
$p=\dfrac h\lambda\propto\dfrac1\lambda\propto\left(\dfrac1{2^2}-\dfrac1{n^2}\right)$.
1st line ($3\to2$): $\dfrac14-\dfrac19=\dfrac5{36}$; 2nd line ($4\to2$): $\dfrac14-\dfrac1{16}=\dfrac3{16}$.
Ratio $=\dfrac{5/36}{3/16}=\dfrac{20}{27}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A LCR series circuit driven with $E_{rms}=90$ V at frequency $f_d=30$ Hz has resistance $R=80\ \Omega$, an inductance with inductive reactance $X_L=20.0\ \Omega$ and capacitance with capacitive reactance $X_C=80.0\ \Omega$. The power factor of the circuit is ______.
questions.sol:
$Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_C-X_L)^2}=\sqrt{80^2+60^2}=100\ \Omega$.
Power factor $=\dfrac RZ=0.8$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Refer to the circuit diagram given below. The heat generated across the 6 $\Omega$ resistance in 100 second is $\dfrac{\alpha}{100}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is ________. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
Take the right junction as $0$ V and let the left junction of the parallel part (after the $3\ \Omega$) be at $x$. With the polarities shown, the left end of the $3\ \Omega$ is at $+2$ V, and the $6\ \Omega$ branch current from left to right is $\dfrac{x-3}{6}$.
KCL at $x$: $\dfrac{2-x}{3}=\dfrac x4+\dfrac{x-3}{6}\Rightarrow8-4x=5x-6\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{14}{9}$ V.
Current in $6\ \Omega$: $\left|\dfrac{x-3}{6}\right|=\dfrac{13}{54}$ A.
Heat in 100 s $=\left(\dfrac{13}{54}\right)^2\times6\times100=\dfrac{101400}{2916}\approx34.77$ J $=\dfrac{3477}{100}$ J.
$\alpha\approx3477$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An unpolarized light of intensity $I_0$ passes through polarizer and then through a certain optically active solution and finally it goes to analyser. If the angle between analyser and polariser is $0^\circ$ and intensity of light emerged from analyser is $\dfrac38I_0$, the angle of rotation of the light by the solution with respect to analyser is ______ degrees.
questions.sol:
After the polariser: $\dfrac{I_0}{2}$. The solution rotates the plane by $\theta$ relative to the analyser.
Malus: $\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^2\theta=\dfrac38I_0\Rightarrow\cos^2\theta=\dfrac34\Rightarrow\theta=30^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The energy released when $\dfrac{7}{17.13}$ kg of $^7_3$Li is converted into $^4_2$He by proton bombardment is $\alpha\times10^{32}$ eV. The value of $\alpha$ is ____. (Nearest integer)
(Mass of $^7_3$Li $=7.0183$ u, mass of $^4_2$He $=4.004$ u, mass of proton $=1.008$ u and 1 u $=931$ MeV/c$^2$ and Avogadro number $=6.0\times10^{23}$)
questions.sol:
$^7_3\mathrm{Li}+{}^1_1\mathrm{H}\to2\,{}^4_2\mathrm{He}$: $\Delta m=7.0183+1.008-8.008=0.0183$ u, $Q=0.0183\times931\approx17.04$ MeV per reaction.
Number of Li nuclei $=\dfrac{7000/17.13}{7}\times6\times10^{23}\approx3.50\times10^{25}$.
Energy $\approx3.50\times10^{25}\times17.04\times10^6$ eV $\approx5.97\times10^{32}$ eV.
$\alpha\approx6$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A three coulomb charge moves from the point $(0,-2,-5)$ to the point $(5,1,2)$ in an electric field expressed as $\vec E=2x\hat i+3y^2\hat j+4\hat k$ N/C. The work done in moving the charge is ______ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A certain gas is isothermally compressed to $\left(\dfrac13\right)^{\text{rd}}$ of its initial volume ($V_0=3$ litre) by applying required pressure. If the bulk modulus of the gas is $3\times10^5$ N/m$^2$, the magnitude of work done on the gas is _____ J.
questions.sol:
For an isothermal process the bulk modulus equals the pressure, $B=p$, so the applied pressure is taken as $p=3\times10^5$ N/m$^2$.
Change in volume $\Delta V=3-1=2$ litre $=2\times10^{-3}$ m$^3$.
$W=p\,\Delta V=3\times10^5\times2\times10^{-3}=600$ J (the official answer).
(Note: this treats the pressure as constant; the exact isothermal work $p_0V_0\ln3$ would be about $989$ J.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.note: The official final key gives 600, which treats the pressure as constant (W = pΔV with p = B). The exact isothermal work is p₀V₀ ln 3 ≈ 989 J; the key is followed for marking.

questions.text:
An oxide of iron contains 69.9% iron, its empirical formula, is:
(Given : Molar mass of Fe and O are 56 and 16 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively.)
questions.sol:
Moles in 100 g: Fe $=\dfrac{69.9}{56}=1.248$, O $=\dfrac{30.1}{16}=1.881$.
Ratio Fe : O $=1:1.507\approx2:3$.
Empirical formula $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$.

questions.text: If shortest wavelength of hydrogen atom in Lyman series is $x$, then longest wavelength in Balmer series of He$^+$ is:
questions.sol:
H, Lyman shortest ($\infty\to1$): $\dfrac1x=R_H$.
He$^+$ ($Z=2$), Balmer longest ($3\to2$): $\dfrac1\lambda=4R_H\left(\dfrac14-\dfrac19\right)=\dfrac{5R_H}{9}$.
$\lambda=\dfrac{9}{5R_H}=\dfrac{9x}{5}$.

questions.text: The pairs among $A=\left[\mathrm{SO_3^{2-},CO_3^{2-}}\right]$, $B=\left[\mathrm{O_2^{2-},F_2}\right]$, $C=\left[\mathrm{CN^-,CO}\right]$, $D=\left[\mathrm{NH_3,H_3O^+}\right]$ and $E=\left[\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-},CrO_4^{2-}}\right]$ that do not have similar Lewis dot structure are
questions.sol:
A: $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$ has a lone pair on S (pyramidal), $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$ has none (planar): not similar.
B: $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{F_2}$ are isoelectronic, single bond with three lone pairs on each atom: similar.
C: $\mathrm{CN^-}$ and CO both have a triple bond and one lone pair on each atom: similar. D: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$: three bonds and one lone pair: similar.
E: $\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}$ (Mn(VI), $d^1$, one unpaired electron) differs from $\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}$ (Cr(VI), $d^0$): not similar.
Answer: A and E.

questions.text:
Arrange the following isothermal processes in order of the magnitude of the work $(p-V)$ involved between states 1 and 2.
A. Expansion in single stage $w_A$
B. Expansion in multi stages $w_B$
C. Compression in single stage $w_C$
D. Compression in multi stages $w_D$
Choose the correct option.
questions.sol:
Expansion work is largest when reversible, so $|w_B|>|w_A|$; compression work is smallest when reversible, so $|w_C|>|w_D|$.
Compression work is always at least the reversible work, and expansion work at most the reversible work, between the same states.
So $|w_C|>|w_D|>|w_B|>|w_A|$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: When 0.25 moles of a non-volatile, non-ionizable solute was dissolved in 1 mole of a solvent the vapor pressure of solution was $x$ % of vapor pressure of pure solvent. What is $x$ %?
questions.sol:
Raoult's law: $\dfrac{p}{p^0}=x_{\text{solvent}}=\dfrac{1}{1+0.25}=0.8$.
$x=80\%$.

questions.text:
One mole each of He and A(g) are taken in a 10 L closed flask and heated to 400 K to establish the following equilibrium.
$\mathrm{A(g)}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{B(g)}$
$K_c$ for this reaction at 400 K is 4.0. The partial pressures (in atm) of He and B(g) are respectively (at equilibrium)
(Assume He, A(g) and B(g) behave as ideal gases)
(Given : R = 0.082 L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
$K_c=\dfrac{[B]}{[A]}=\dfrac{x}{1-x}=4\Rightarrow x=0.8$ mol B.
$\dfrac{RT}{V}=\dfrac{0.082\times400}{10}=3.28$ atm per mol.
$p_{He}=1\times3.28=3.28$ atm; $p_B=0.8\times3.28=2.624$ atm.

questions.text:
Consider the following data.
Electrolyte$\Lambda^\circ_m$ (S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$)
$\mathrm{BaCl_2}$$x_1$
$\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$$x_2$
HCl$x_3$
$\mathrm{BaSO_4}$ is sparingly soluble in water. If the conductivity of the saturated $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$ solution is $x$ S cm$^{-1}$ then the solubility product of $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$ can be given as
(Here $\Lambda_m=\Lambda^\circ_m$)
questions.sol:
Kohlrausch: $\Lambda^\circ_m(\mathrm{BaSO_4})=\Lambda^\circ_m(\mathrm{BaCl_2})+\Lambda^\circ_m(\mathrm{H_2SO_4})-2\Lambda^\circ_m(\mathrm{HCl})=x_1+x_2-2x_3$.
Solubility $s=\dfrac{1000\,\kappa}{\Lambda_m}=\dfrac{10^3x}{x_1+x_2-2x_3}$ mol L$^{-1}$.
$K_{sp}=s^2=\dfrac{10^6x^2}{(x_1+x_2-2x_3)^2}$, which is option (1) with the degree of dissociation $\alpha=1$ (since $\Lambda_m=\Lambda^\circ_m$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Aluminium is more electropositive than thallium as the standard electrode potential value of $E^\circ_{\mathrm{Al^{3+}/Al}}$ is negative and $E^\circ_{\mathrm{Tl^{3+}/Tl}}$ is positive.
Statement II: The sum of first three ionization enthalpies of boron is very high when compared to that of aluminium. Due to this reason boron forms covalent compounds only and aluminium forms $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ ion.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: $E^\circ_{\mathrm{Al^{3+}/Al}}=-1.66$ V and $E^\circ_{\mathrm{Tl^{3+}/Tl}}=+1.26$ V, so Al readily forms $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ and is more electropositive: true.
Statement II: boron's very high $\Delta_iH_1+\Delta_iH_2+\Delta_iH_3$ prevents $\mathrm{B^{3+}}$, so boron forms only covalent compounds; Al, with lower values, forms $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$: true.
Both statements are true.

The correct statements among the following are.
A. Basic vanadium oxide is used in the manufacture of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$.
B. The spin-only magnetic moment value of the transition metal halide employed in Ziegler-Natta polymerization is 2.84 BM.
C. The p-block metal compound employed in Ziegler-Natta polymerization has the metal in +3 oxidation state.
D. The number of electrons present in the outer most 'd' orbital of metal halide employed in Wacker process is 8.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ (contact process) is amphoteric, not a basic oxide: false.
B: $\mathrm{TiCl_4}$ has $\mathrm{Ti^{4+}}$ ($3d^0$), spin-only moment 0: false.
C: $\mathrm{Al(C_2H_5)_3}$ has Al in +3 state: true.
D: $\mathrm{PdCl_2}$ has $\mathrm{Pd^{2+}}$ ($4d^8$): true.
C and D only.

questions.text:
Which of the following are true about the energy of the given d-orbitals of a tetrahedral complex?
A. $d_{xy}=d_{xz}>d_{x^2-y^2}$
B. $d_{xy}=d_{yz}>d_{z^2}$
C. $d_{x^2-y^2}>d_{z^2}>d_{xz}$
D. $d_{x^2-y^2}=d_{z^2}<d_{xz}$
Choose the correct answer from the given below:
questions.sol:
In a tetrahedral field the $t_2$ set ($d_{xy},d_{yz},d_{xz}$) lies above the degenerate $e$ set ($d_{x^2-y^2},d_{z^2}$).
A, B and D agree with this; C is false ($d_{x^2-y^2}=d_{z^2}$, both below $d_{xz}$).
A, B and D only.

questions.text: $R_f$ value for 2-methylpropene in a solvent system (Ethyl acetate + ether) is 0.42. 2-methylpropene is treated with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ to give major organic product (X). $R_f$ value for (X) in the same solvent system under identical condition will be:
questions.sol:
Acid-catalysed hydration (Markovnikov) gives X $=$ tert-butyl alcohol, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3COH}$.
The alcohol is far more polar than the alkene and is held more strongly by the stationary phase, so it moves less.
Its $R_f$ must be lower than 0.42: 0.12.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: 2,6-diethylcyclohexanone and 6-methyl-2-n-propylcyclohexanone are metamers.
Statement II: 2,2,6,6 - tetramethylcyclohexanone exhibits keto-enol tautomerism.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: both are $\mathrm{C_{10}H_{18}O}$ ketones that differ only in the alkyl groups on the two sides of the C=O group (ethyl/ethyl versus methyl/n-propyl): metamers, true.
Statement II: in 2,2,6,6-tetramethylcyclohexanone both $\alpha$-carbons carry no hydrogen, so no enol can form: false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Methane can be prepared by decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate, Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate and reaction of $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}$ with water.
Statement II: Methane cannot be prepared from unsaturated hydrocarbons and by Wurtz reaction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: decarboxylation of $\mathrm{CH_3COONa}$ (soda lime) and $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}+\mathrm{H_2O}$ give methane, but Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate gives ethane: false.
Statement II: hydrogenation of alkenes/alkynes gives at least ethane, and Wurtz coupling gives at least ethane: true.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: 3-phenylpropene reacts with HBr and gives secondary alkyl bromide having a chiral carbon atom as the major product.
Statement II: Aryl chlorides and aryl cyanides can be prepared by Sandmeyer reaction as well as Gattermann reaction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CH{=}CH_2}+\mathrm{HBr}\to\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CHBrCH_3}$ (Markovnikov), a secondary bromide whose C-2 carries H, Br, $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_2C_6H_5}$: chiral, true.
Statement II: aryl chlorides can be made by both reactions, but the Gattermann reaction (Cu/HX) is used for aryl chlorides and bromides, not aryl cyanides (CuCN, Sandmeyer): false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions
$$\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C{-}OH}\ \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) H}^+\text{, PhCOOH}]{\text{(i) Cu / 573K}}\ \mathrm{P}$$The major product P is:
questions.sol:
Tertiary alcohols are dehydrated by Cu at 573 K: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3COH}\to\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}CH_2}$ (2-methylpropene).
With $\mathrm{H^+}$ the alkene gives the tert-butyl carbocation, which alkylates the ring of benzoic acid.
COOH is a meta-directing group, so P is 3-tert-butylbenzoic acid, option (2).

questions.text:
Arrange the following compounds according to increasing order of boiling points.
n - $\mathrm{C_4H_9OH}$ (A), n - $\mathrm{C_4H_9NH_2}$ (B), n - $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}$ (C) and $\mathrm{C_2H_5NHC_2H_5}$ (D).

n-Butane has no hydrogen bonding (lowest). Diethylamine (2$^\circ$, one N-H) bonds less than n-butylamine (1$^\circ$, two N-H). O-H hydrogen bonds are the strongest, so n-butanol is highest.
Approximate b.p.: C (273 K) < D (329 K) < B (351 K) < A (391 K).
C < D < B < A.

questions.text:
First and second ionization enthalpies of lithium are 520 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and 7297 kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. Energy required to convert 3.5 mg lithium (g) into $\mathrm{Li^{2+}(g)}$ $[\mathrm{Li(g)}\to\mathrm{Li^{2+}(g)}]$ is ________ kJ mol$^{-1}$. (nearest integer)
[Molar mass of Li $=7$ g mol$^{-1}$]

Moles of Li $=\dfrac{3.5\times10^{-3}}{7}=5\times10^{-4}$ mol.

questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions.
The percentage of nitrogen in the yellow product (X) formed is ________%. (Nearest Integer)
(Given Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H:1, C:12, N:14)
questions.sol:
Diazoaminobenzene $\mathrm{C_6H_5N{=}N{-}NHC_6H_5}$ rearranges in acid with excess aniline (warm) to p-aminoazobenzene, $\mathrm{C_6H_5N{=}NC_6H_4NH_2}$, a yellow dye = X.

questions.text:
4.7 g of phenol is heated with Zn to give product X. If this reaction goes to 60% completion then the number of moles of compound X formed will be ____ $\times10^{-2}$. (Nearest Integer)
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ : H:1, C:12, O:16)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_6H_5OH}+\mathrm{Zn}\to\mathrm{C_6H_6}+\mathrm{ZnO}$, so X is benzene (1 : 1).
Moles of phenol $=\dfrac{4.7}{94}=0.05$.
At 60% completion: $0.6\times0.05=0.03=3\times10^{-2}$ mol.

questions.text:
Sucrose hydrolyses in acidic medium into glucose and fructose by first order rate law with $t_{1/2}=3$ hour. The percentage of sucrose remaining after 6 hours is _____. (Nearest integer)
(Given : log 2 = 0.3010 and log 3 = 0.4771)
questions.sol:
6 hours $=2$ half-lives.
Fraction remaining $=\left(\dfrac12\right)^2=\dfrac14$, i.e. $25\%$.

questions.text:
Consider the reaction $\mathrm{X}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{Y}$ at 300 K. If $\Delta H^\theta$ and K are 28.40 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $1.8\times10^{-7}$ at the same temperature, then the magnitude of $\Delta S^\theta$ for the reaction in J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$ is________. (Nearest integer)
(Given : R = 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, ln 10 = 2.3, log 3 = 0.48, log 2 = 0.30)
questions.sol:
$\log(1.8\times10^{-7})=\log2+2\log3-7-1=0.30+0.96-8=-6.74$, so $\ln K=2.3\times(-6.74)=-15.502$.
$\Delta G^\theta=-RT\ln K=8.3\times300\times15.502\approx38600$ J mol$^{-1}$.
$\Delta S^\theta=\dfrac{\Delta H^\theta-\Delta G^\theta}{T}=\dfrac{28400-38600}{300}=-34$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.
Magnitude $=34$.
